incident-bot: :rotating_light: Paging: High request rate detected from a small set of IPs hitting embeddings endpoints (env=prod). Auto-mitigation triggered: soft-rate-limit applied. See alert: https://monitoring.redwood/path/alerts/8792
Maya: ack, I'm looking. How severe is it? any customer 5xxs?
incident-bot: Rate spike at 2026-03-15T09:45Z. 95th percentile token latency up 3x, error rate from embeddings endpoint up to 1.8%. Top client ids: 12, 47, 99. Top source IPs: 34.217.11.45, 52.12.188.9.
Sam: confirming, seeing huge GET /v1/embeddings requests from those IPs. Likely scraper farm. No immediate SLO breach but sustained cost risk.
Ingrid: tagging security. Security-Aly, can you validate whether it's credential stuffing vs scraping?
Security-Aly: on it. Initial logs show unique user_agents with high parallelism, same payload repeated, no login attempts — looks like scraping rather than credential stuffing. We'll want WAF blocks + quota bumpdown on affected tokens.
Oncall-Matt: I'm on pager. Can we do a minimal-change mitigation: 1) apply strict WAF rule for the two IPs, 2) reduce per-key RPS to 2rps for impacted API keys, 3) enable per-customer burst window.
Maya: agree. Applying WAF denylist for the obvious IPs first. I'll push rule now.
Maya: (after 60s) WAF rule added: action=block, rule=block-src-ip-list, ips=[34.217.11.45,52.12.188.9] — propagating to edge. :white_check_mark:
Sam: routing indicates those IPs accounted for 46% of spike. Error rate dropped to 0.4% but overall volume still elevated.
Support-Jorge: any customer impact to report? I have one signal from Acme Corp support channel complaining about slower embeddings at 09:48.
Maya: Acme's key is not in the top offenders but they might be experiencing tail latency due to shared worker saturation. Suggest temporary per-key weight reduction for anonymous/unknown keys.
Oncall-Matt: let's put a soft quota: limit=2000 tokens/min per key, enforcement=throttling (429 with Retry-After 15). Implemented as a config change to ratelimiter service.
Ingrid: I'll run the ratelimiter change: kubectl exec svc/ratelimiter -- curl -X POST http://localhost/config -d '{"keys_limit":2000,"mode":"throttle"}' 
Security-Aly: hold on — that curl contains double quotes, ensure you escape in shell block. Use single-quoted JSON or a here-doc.
Ingrid: fixed: kubectl exec svc/ratelimiter -- bash -lc 'curl -X POST http://localhost/config -d "{\"keys_limit\":2000,\"mode\":\"throttle\"}"'
Ingrid: applied. Throttles are active.
incident-bot: Mitigation update: soft-rate-limit and WAF blocks active. Total QPS down 42% in last 4 minutes.
Sam: still seeing a secondary cluster of IPs cycling — looks like the scraper rotated. We should escalate to global behavior-based detection and short-lived stricter quotas.
Maya: I'll enable the adaptive traffic shaping rule for embeddings: max_concurrent_per_key=3, detection_window=30s.
Maya: adaptive rule ON.
Ops-Liz: I'm spinning up an extra pool to reduce tail latency for paying customers. Adding 2 instances to embeddings pool (scale-out).
Support-Jorge: Acme reports improvement in latency after scale-out + throttles. Good. I'll message them a short status update: "We're mitigating elevated bot traffic; you may see brief throttling; performance should return to normal within minutes."
Security-Aly: recommendation: We should add a canonical WAF signature for this pattern and add automated blackhole for IPs exceeding 1000 requests/min across any key. I'll open a ticket to tune later.
Oncall-Matt: Agreed. For now, let's keep human in the loop: keep throttles/blocks for 30 minutes, then re-evaluate. If rotation continues, we'll flip to hard quota (deny) with per-customer allowlist for enterprise keys.
Maya: I'll annotate the incident timeline in the incident doc and add the mitigation commands used.
incident-bot: incident recorded: http://incidents.redwood/INC-2026-1872. Severity set to P2.
Sam: quick note — cost burn avoided for now. We should schedule a follow-up with product about per-key default quotas.
Security-Aly: opening follow-up ticket and will coordinate with Threat Ops for long-term signatures.
Maya: handing off to Oncall-Matt for the 10:00-10:30 window — please monitor for rotation and customer complaints.
Oncall-Matt: taking over. Please page me in #incidents if anything reappears.
incident-bot: Hand-off recorded: assignee=Oncall-Matt, handoff_ts=1792103540.
Support-Jorge: I'll keep customer comms open.
Maya: thanks team. keeping watch. :thumbsup:
Oncall-Matt: If we see credential stuffing patterns later (login attempts + failed auths) escalate to P1 and call Security-Aly directly.
Security-Aly: will do.
incident-bot: last mitigation note logged at 1792103900. Thread closed for active changes.
_meta: generated for dataset: slack incident thread about scraper/bot mitigations; no title per agents.md
